issues.detail: The Greek 'μηδεν σοι' (nothing to you) is rendered as 'Đừng làm gì' (Do nothing). In context, the wife is telling the man not to do anything *to* the righteous man. However, the Vietnamese phrasing 'Đừng làm gì đến người công bình đó' can be interpreted as a general command not to do anything, whereas the Greek specifically addresses the man ('toi').

The Greek 'καθημενου δε αυτου' specifies that while he was *sitting* on the judgment seat/bench. The Vietnamese translation 'Khi người đang ngồi trên tòa án' captures the action but loses the specific nuance of the 'judgment seat' (βήματος) context, though this is a minor stylistic point. More importantly, the Greek 'δι αυτον' (because of him/on his account) is rendered as 'vì cớ người', which is acceptable.
